 Ranking college basketball's top newcomers: Kansas' Tyran Stokes earns Freshman of the Week honors
 A look at the top-performing freshmen in college basketball last week and for the 2026-27 season
 By
 Cameron Salerno 
 Nov 17, 2026
 at
 10:02 am ET 
 •
 3 min read
 Getty Images 
 It was rare for a player of Tyran Stokes caliber to be uncommitted so late in the recruiting cycle. The top-ranked player in the 2026 recruiting class waited until April to announce his commitment to Kansas over Kentucky, which gave Bill Self his third No. 1 overall recruit in his coaching tenure with the Jayhawks.
 That's why last week's win over Kentucky was "personal" for Stokes. The projected No. 1 overall pick in the 2027 NBA Draft , who is from Louisville, explained why the second leg of the Champions Classic meant a little extra because of the team his Kansas squad faced.
 "For me, it was up to Kansas and Kentucky for my last two schools," Stokes said. "I'm from Louisville. I had a long recruiting process with Kentucky, so obviously when I chose Kansas, and I knew that game was going to be here, it was personal for sure."
 Stokes finished with his first double-double (23 points and 10 rebounds) of his college career. The 23 points he scored during the 89-69 win over Kentucky matched the same amount of points he scored during the first two games of the season against Fordham and Middle Tennessee.
 Because of that performance, Stokes is our Freshman of the Week and is No. 1 in our updated Frosh Ranking. Let's jump in and get to why Stokes is our second winner of the CBS Sports/USBWA Freshman of the Week for the 2026-27 college basketball season.
 Freshman of the Week: Tyran Stokes, Kansas
 Welcome back to the Frosh Watch, our weekly ranking of the five most impressive freshmen in college basketball. For the 12th season in a row, CBS Sports has once again teamed up with the United States Basketball Writers Association and its Wayman Tisdale Freshman of the Year Award to present this every-Tuesday feature. Each week, we'll start by announcing the national Freshman of the Week honoree. The cycle for FOTW runs Tuesday-Monday. 
 Stokes was fantastic on both ends of the floor during Kansas' statement win over Kentucky. In total, Stokes finished with 23 points, 10 rebounds, four assists, a block and a steal. Stokes also knocked down four 3-pointers and hit all three of his free-throw attempts after starting the season 8-of-14 from the line.
 Self had high praise for his star freshman  after the win.
 Projected No. 1 pick Tyran Stokes put up a double-double against No. 24 Kentucky 👀🔥
23 PTS | 4-8 3PT | 10 REB | 4 AST pic.twitter.com/FBHDYIZqey 
— B/R Hoops (@brhoops) November 11, 2026 
 "I actually thought he handled the moment better than I actually anticipated him doing," Self said. "He's very emotional, which is a big, big plus. Nobody should take that as a negative. But I didn't want him to be too geeked up where he couldn't play. What helped him a lot tonight was seeing that first 3 go down. After that, I thought he played under control. I thought he played within what we're trying to do, and still found a way to be aggressive at the same time. I thought it was pretty impressive."
 Previous Freshman of the Week winners
 Nov. 10: Nikola Kusturica, UCLA 
 1. Tyran Stokes | F | Kansas
 Stats : 15.3 PPG | 7.3 RPG | 2.3 APG 
 Stokes had his best performance of the season in a perfect spot against Kentucky. Through the first three games of his college career, Stokes has showcased his ability to use his frame to draw contact and get to the free-throw line. Stokes is also a very underrated passer.  Last week: 2
 2. Nikola Kusturica | F | UCLA
 Stats : 18.3 PPG | 4.7 RPG | 2.7 APG 
 Kusturica has been everything UCLA hoped he would be and more through the first two weeks of the season. He finished with 17 points, three rebounds and three assists in just 22 minutes during a blowout win over Arkansas-Pine Bluff. Even when he's not scoring, he can impact the game.  Last week:  1
 3. Caleb Holt | G | Arizona
 Stats : 17.3 PPG | 7.3 RPG | 1.3 APG 
 Holt is coming off his best game at the college level against Auburn. The Huntsville, Alabama, native finished with 24 points, nine rebounds and five steals during the 80-69 win. Holt is a terrific rebounder for his size and is a true two-way player.  Last week:  NR
 Alabama native Caleb Holt against Auburn on the road:
24 PTS | 4-6 3PT | 9 REB | 5 STL
The star freshman was huge tonight for No. 12 Arizona pic.twitter.com/y5E2zapOh8 
— B/R Hoops (@brhoops) November 14, 2026 
 4. Miles Sadler | G | West Virginia
 Stats : 17.7 PPG | 1.7 RPG | 7.0 APG 
 Sadler finished with 12 points and six assists during a 14-point win over Mercer last week. Sadler and West Virginia have a test coming up against Auburn on Tuesday in the opening round of the Player Era 8.  Last week:  3
 West Virginia Freshman PG Miles Sadler has been one of the best prospects in the 2027 NBA Draft so far this season. 
Through his first three games Sadler is averaging 18/2/7 and 1.3 steals a game, while shooting 52% from the field in 26 MPG. 
Sadler is one of the best… pic.twitter.com/NI0auvZOTL 
— KJ (@KJScouting) November 13, 2026 
 5. Quentin Coleman | G | Illinois
 Stats : 15.5 PPG | 6.5 RPG | 4.5 APG 
 Coleman finished with 19 points, five rebounds and four assists during Illinois' loss to Texas Tech on the road. He also made a big impact during Illinois' win over Sam Houston State by recording 11 points, eight rebounds, six assists and four steals.  Last week:  5
 6’4 Illinois Freshman PG Quentin Coleman has been one of the best prospects in this season’s NBA Draft so far this season.
